annotations.text:
SIGN IN - Option B, built out.

Copy is the APPROVED brand line "See the move before the league does." - the line WelcomeView.swift already carries, inherited by the screen that absorbs it. The alternate approved line is "See the result before it happens." (page-system, the primary marketing line). Say the word and I swap it.

The Welcome screen is GONE. This is the first screen, and Demo lives on it.

The mark is your REAL stacked lockup from logos/svg/omen-lockup-stacked.svg - the O is already a football with a brass sheen, so the ball is the logo rather than a decoration beside it.

Football, kept serious: faint yard lines across the ground and a single warm glow behind the mark. No turf texture, no cartoon.

Apple is the filled primary because guideline 4.8 requires Sign in with Apple to be at least as prominent as Google or Discord on iOS. On ANDROID the primary swaps to Google.

The three icon buttons carry aria-labels - an icon-only control is unusable with VoiceOver without them.

BUILD FROM ROSTERS — the path that doesn't exist today.

Real assets from real rosters, so nothing can be traded that isn't owned. Third team is a chip, not a mode.

The dash on Kraft is deliberate: no provider rank Omen can stand behind, so it shows a dash and never invents one.

THE READ — one screen, three separations.

1. The verdict is blunt and scored ('Counter' + Confident band).
2. The counter is CONCRETE, built from assets that actually exist.
3. Private advice is fenced — Mike's RB thinness never leaves this screen.

'Launch Sleeper' is demoted and labelled honestly: it opens the app and nothing more. Sleeper publishes no trade-write endpoint, so COPY is the real product.

SHARE CARD — the poll is CUT.

No vote endpoint or storage ever existed; the earlier '42 votes' was fiction at a scale a 10-team league never reaches. People argue in the group chat they're already in.

What's left is the thing that travels: an image and a link carrying the trade and NOTHING else — no verdict, no leverage, no read on Mike.

SWIPE DECK, not a scroll.

One advisor at a time, next one peeking. Impact orders the deck, so Waiver leads this week.

Two things this buys: each seat gets a real headline and a real action instead of a squeezed row, and 'only advisors with something to say' now shortens the DECK rather than leaving gaps.

SWIPED TO SEAT 2.

Same frame, different card. Dots carry position.

OPEN: a carousel hides content. If someone never swipes, they never see the Ledger. Worth deciding whether the deck auto-advances once, or whether seat 3 is allowed to be missed.

CONFIDENCE — bands, never a percentage.

Confident / Leaning / Coin flip. The three-up strip is here to show the states side by side; the real screen shows only the active band.

Drop the strip once you've picked the treatment.

WAIVER lives in League: Matchup - Standings - Waiver - Activity.

Every pickup names its drop. The engine picks it; the model only writes the sentence.

The deadline chip is load-bearing — under pure-impact ordering it is the ONLY warning a closing claim gets.

LEDGER — self-reported rows count, but are marked ('You told us').

That forces the record to disclose its own composition: '5-1 when you followed' sits beside 'two of these six are your own report.'

No blended number without that sentence.

QUIET WEEK — the playful register, fenced.

Never after a loss, an injury, or an error. A single fixed line reads as a stuck screen by the fifth viewing; if it wears thin, rotate a small set in the same voice rather than going flat.

ABBY'S SCREEN — signed in, no league.

The context strip becomes the connect prompt and follows her everywhere until it's done. Providers by market share, per your call.

Demo mode is gone, so there is no 'try it fake' escape hatch here.

THE HIGHEST-STAKES SCREEN IN THE APP.

Three plain promises before the sheet opens — this is what separates 'signing into ESPN' from 'a scam asking for my password'. Modelled on Plaid Link.

BLOCKED until the ESPN terms read and App Review answer are written down (W1-GATE).

BETA ONLY — compiled out of App Store builds by a build flag, not a runtime toggle.

The 'sent with your report' list is deliberately visible: people share more when they can see exactly what leaves their phone.
